newsitem.title: USA: CBO says 10-year U.S. budget outlook much brighter.
newsitem.headline: CBO says 10-year U.S. budget outlook much brighter.

text.p: A 10-year budget outlook to be released by the Congressional Budget Office in coming days will show baseline federal deficits one-third lower than CBO projections last May, a CBO official said Wednesday.

In testimony before the Senate Budget Committee, CBO Deputy Director James Blum also said a short-term deal to balance the budget by 2002 would not solve the long-term problems facing the U.S. economy due to growth of entitlement programs such as Medicare and Social Security.
"Our new 10-year baseline deficits will be one-third lower than what we projected last May," Blum told the panel.
He urged lawmakers not to wait too long to make structural changes in politically popular entitlements, including Medicare, Social Security and Medicaid.
"Whatever policy actions are taken, they ought to be taken soon," Blum said. "Doing nothing about the long-term deficits looming on the horizon is not a feasible option."
He said a balanced budget was not vital as long as Congress limited spending growth and prevented deficits from growing dramatically.
